sentences.text: THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 21.03.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.585/2009 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER, ADDITIONAL MACT, RAMANAGARA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENCING AT KALABURAGI, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 21-03- 2012 passed in MVC No.585/2009 by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member Additional MACT, Ramanagara, whereby the petition came to be allowed in part and a sum of Rs.2,93,420/- has been awarded as compensation holding that respondent Nos. 2 and 3 therein are liable to pay compensation and dismissing the petition against respondent No.1, the petitioner has approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement urging various grounds.
2. The parties would be referred to as per their ranks before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. The brief facts are as below:

On 01-09-2009 the petitioner and his brother were proceeding on the left side of the road on Hero Honda Passion motor cycle bearing No.KA-42-E-7483 in order to go to Attilakkamma Temple in Tumkur District.

When they reached near the cross of Sombenahalli Bayalu at about 1.15 p.m., a bus bearing No.KA-01-F-3244 came from Magadi side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle causing the accident wherein both the petitioner and rider of the motor cycle fell down and suffered grievous injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Govt.
hospital Magadi and then Rajarajeswari Medical College and Hospital, then to NIMHANS and he took treatment by spending Rs.2,00,000/- at HOSMAT hospital.
Even now, he is having pain and unable to perform his normal activities.
The police have filed a criminal case in Cr.No.403/2009 in respect of that accident.

Further, it is the case of the petitioner that, respondent No.3 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the bus and petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,00,000/-
Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/
2 from them and prayed to allow the petition.
4. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, respondent No.1 though appeared through counsel, has not filed any objections and respondent No.3 remained exparte.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2-Insurance Company has filed written statement contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and it is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and denied all the allegation that bus driver is responsible for the accident.
It is its case that the petitioner lost control over the bike and skidded off the road and motor cycle rider was not holding valid driving licence.

In view of the same,
the respondent No.2 alleges that the motor cycle rider himself is responsible for the accident.

It is the further case of respondent No.2 that, it has issued policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of bus bearing No.KA.01.F.3244 and its liability is as per the terms and conditions of the policy and prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings and contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues for its consideration.

Before the Tribunal, petitioner got examined himself as PW1,
got examined two witnesses as PWs 2 and 3 and got marked Exs.P1 to P88.
Respondents did not adduce or produce any oral or documentary evidence.

6. On hearing both the sides and considering the materials available on record, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition against respondent Nos. 2 and 3 and dismissed the petition against respondent No.1 and awarded a sum of Rs.2,93,420/- as compensation under different heads and as under:
1 Attendants Charges Rs. 3,000/-
2 Pain and suffering Rs. 35,000/-

3 Loss of future income Rs.1,55,520/-
4

Medical Expenses Rs. 71,800/-
5 Loss of future comforts and amenties Rs. 10,000/- 6 Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 9,000/- 7

Transportation Charges Rs 9,100/-
Total Rs.2,93,420/-
7.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal seeking enhancement.
8. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels in pursuant to the notice issued by this Court and the Tribunal records have been secured.

9. Heard Sri K.Shantharaj, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner, Sri O. Mahesh, learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company/respondent No.1 Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/
3 and Sri K. Nagaraj, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 and perused the Tribunal records.
10. Aggrieved by the judgment of the Tribunal on the quantum, the petitioner has come up in this appeal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The original respondent Nos. 2 and 3 before the Tribunal have not filed any appeal or cross objections.
Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 before the Tribunal are arrayed as the respondent No.1 and 2 in this appeal.
The fact that there was an accident and chargesheet filed against the driver of the bus owned by the respondent No.1 herein is not in dispute.
On the bases of the chargesheet, the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.

The fact that the vehicle was covered with the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2/ insurance company is also being an admitted fact, there is no necessity to consider the said aspect any more.

11. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/petitioner has contended that the Tribunal has not considered the injuries suffered by the petitioner in a proper perspective and future loss of income has not been properly assessed by it.
In furtherance of his contention, he submits that the income of the petitioner should have been considered at a higher rate and also that the loss of amenities awarded is on the lower side.
He contends that the loss of income during the laid up period is also not properly assessed by the Tribunal and therefore, there is a need for reassessment of the quantum of the compensation amount.
Per contra the learned counsels appearing for the respondants have defended the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal as adequate.
12. The records reveal that the petitioner had sustained closed proximal fracture of 1/3rd of the right tibia and inter phalangeal joint.

The Doctor, who was examined by the petitioner as PW2 has stated that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital on 1-9-2009 and he underwent open reduction and internal fixation with condyle plate (six holed) of right proximal tibia on 2-9-2009 and was discharged on 3-9-2009.
He further stated that again petitioner was admitted on 12-11-2010 and implants were removed and he was discharged on 15-11-2010.
He further states that there is a permanent disability and the middle finger of the right hand cannot be extended completely and there is fixed flexion deformity.
He also states that the middle finger and inter phalangeal joint is restricted and there is also pain with swelling over the right knee joint and also the ankle joint.
Therefore, there is permanent disability to the petitioner.
Admittedly, he comes to the conclusion that there is a disability of 9% of the upper limb and 45% disability of the right lower limb and total disability is assessed by the PW2 is at 20%.
The Tribunal has taken the disability at 18%.

The Tribunal has held that the petitioner was aged about 32 years and therefore, the proper multiplier would be '16'.
13.
Coming to the income of the petitioner, the petitioner has stated that he was working as a Manager at Prakruthi Stones and earning Rs.7,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has examined Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 the owner of the said company as PW3 and Ex.P81-salary certificate is produced by him.
The Ex.P81 is on the letter head and the Tribunal has not considered the same though PW3 has been - 10 - examined in this regard.
Ultimately, the Tribunal holds that the income of the petitioner was Rs.4,500/- per month.

The Tribunal holds that petitioner has suffered permanent disability and future loss of income would be Rs.4,500 x 12 x 16 x 18% = 1,55,520/-.
14.
The evidence of the PW3 -Suresh Raje Aras shows that the appellant was working as a Manager and also as a worker.
The cross- examination of PW3 shows that the nature of work of the appellant has not been elicited in detail.
The evidence of the PW 3 shows that he had employed only a few employees and he had not kept the records for payment of the wages/salary.
No such documents are produced.
But the cross examination of the PW 3 is only of denial.
It cannot be lost sight of the fact that smaller business establishments seldom keep the Wage Register and such other records.
Considering the age of the petitioner, it is evident that he was Manager and had developed certain skill commensurate with his age.

Therefore, instead of the notional income of - 11 - Rs.4,500/- considered by the Tribunal, it would be proper to hold that the income was Rs.6,000/-
per month.

15. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that future prospects of the income has not been considered at 40% in view of the fact that petitioner was aged about 32 years and working as a Manager in Prakruthi Stones which is involved in granite business.
On this ground he submits that the future prospects also should have been considered by the Tribunal.
16. The Apex Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs Kahlon @

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs Kahlon @
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Jasmail Singh Kahlon (deceased) through his Legal representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan and another1 has observed in para Nos. 19 and 20 as below:
"19.
In Parminder Singh (supra) compensation on the basis of complete loss of income, the percentage of disability, future prospects were granted applying the relevant multiplier.
Again, in Kajal (supra) the injured was assessed as 100 per cent disabled, considering all of which compensation was awarded on the notional future prospects along with relevant multiplier.
The loss of income to the injured in the facts of the present case has to be assessed 2021 SCC Online SC 691 - 12 - at 75%.
In view of Raj Kumar (supra) there shall be no deduction towards personal expenses.

Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/
5 20.

entities.text: Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We see no reason to deviate from the consistent judicial view taken by more than one High Court that loss of estate would include expenditure on medicines,
treatment, diet, attendant, Doctor's fee, etc. including income and future prospects which would have caused reasonable accretion to the estate but for the sudden expenditure which had to be met from and depleted the estate of the injured,
subsequently deceased."

17. The said decision of the Apex Court was fortified by another decision of the Apex Court in the case of Paraminder Singh Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited and others2, wherein, it was held in para 5 that, "when the disability was 100%, the future prospects are also to be included while assessing the compensation towards future loss of income."

entities.text: Paraminder Singh Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Kumar Vs. Ashok Kumar and another3 has also considered this aspect and in case of the severe injuries, the future prospects are also to be considered by the Tribunal.

entities.text: Sanjay Kumar Vs. Ashok Kumar and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is to be noticed that the future prospects are considered by the Courts whenever the nature of the injuries are severe and resulting disability is almost 100%.
(2019) 7 SCC 217 (2014) 5 Supreme Court Cases 330 - 13 -

When the disability is lesser, and the effect of the disability tapers off over a period of time on account of adaptation of the life style of the injured, it would not be justifiable to award the compensation by escalating the income with future prospects.

Thus, it is evident that in exceptional circumstances, if it is established that the disability is going to affect future prospects of the petitioner, even in injury cases, the said analogy has to be applied.

18. In a case on hand, the learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant/petitioner was working as a Manager in Prakruthi Stones and he had joined the services few months back prior to the incident.
Under these circumstances, I do not find any reasons to apply the principles laid down in the above decision regarding the future prospects.
Thus, the income of the petitioner taken at Rs.4,500/- per month by the Tribunal has to be enhanced to Rs.6,000/-.
Hence, the future loss of income is calculated as: Rs.6000 x 12 x 16 x 18% = 2,07,360/-.
Coming to the compensation awarded under the head of pain and sufferings, it is evident that the petitioner had sustained the injury which has resulted in a disability of 18%.

Under these circumstances, the compensation under the head of pain and sufferings awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.35,000/- appears to be on the lower side and therefore, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

20. The loss of income during the laid up period has been considered by the Tribunal at 2 months and in the considered opinion of this Court and also considering the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant, it would be just and proper to hold that the petitioner was unable to resume his work atleast for a period of three months.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.18,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/
6 21.

sentences.text: The compensation awarded under the head of attendant charges, medical expenses and transportation and other charges do not require any enhancement.

The compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal under the head of loss of future comforts and amenities, in the considered opinion of this court, the loss of amenities should require an enhancement and therefore, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

23. Hence, the compensation is reassessed as below:
1

Attendants Charges Rs. 3,000/-
2 Pain and suffering Rs. 40,000/-

3 Loss of future income Rs. 2,07,360/-
4

Medical Expenses Rs. 71,800/-
5 Loss of future comforts and amentias Rs. 20,000/- 6 Loss of income during laid up period Rs. 18,000/- 7

Transportation Charges Rs 9,100/-
 Total Rs. 3,69,260/-
 Less: awarded by the Tribunal Rs. 2,93,420/-

Enhancement Rs. 75,840/-
24.
Thus, the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.75,840/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part - 16 - (ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 21.03.2012 passed in MVC No.585/2009 by the Tribunal is modified by enhancing the compensation of Rs.75,840/- together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment.

(ii) Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount including the enhanced compensation together with interest within a period of 4 weeks from the Sri Prabhakar T vs The United India Insurance Co., Ltd on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81904443/
7 date of receipt of the copy of this order.
